newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends up vs dollar in Shanghai on holiday eve.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends up vs dollar in Shanghai on holiday eve.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up at a 20-month high of 8.2918 on Thursday from Wednesday's 8.2924 against the U.S. dollar on the Shanghai-based China national foreign exchange interbank market.
Trading was extremely dull on this last trading day before the Chinese lunar new year holiday, traders said.
The market will close from Friday until next Wednesday.
The yuan opened up at an intraday low of 8.2925 and moved up steadily for most of the session, hitting a high of 8.2829 in late trading. Most transactions were done at 8.2920, traders said.

One dealer said the yuan was easily pushed up because volume was so thin. "But there was also a little selling late in the session to prevent the yuan from closing above the key 8.2900 resistance level," he said.
A second dealer said the currency was likely to move around the 8.2920 level in slow trading once the market reopened.
The yuan closed down at an intraday low of 6.6900 from 6.7500 against 100 Japanese yen and up at 1.0680 from 1.0700 against the Hong Kong dollar. Trading was dull, traders said.
